This one is mostly about speed and looks. With every effect on, Telescope now needs about a third of the processor it used to and both apps got a full redesign.

## Faster

- With every effect on at 4K my 8 core Ryzen went from about 3.4 cores busy to 1.1 and the stream holds 30 fps instead of dropping to around 22. A frame gets through all the effects in 15 ms instead of 42.
- At 1080p with everything on it's half the processor it was and at 4K it uses about 700 MB less memory.
- Starting without opening Settings uses about 50 MB less, since Settings is only built the first time you open it.
- Hardware decoding is on by default on Linux with an AMD or Intel graphics card, even if you had it off before. It falls back to the processor automatically if it can't keep up. Windows and NVIDIA cards stay off by default, and **Hardware acceleration** under Video in Settings turns it off.

## New look

I rebuilt the desktop window from scratch. The visual hierarchy is rethought so the controls that matter stand out, the cards have an icon rail, sliders fill to show what they mean and the camera controls are dials. Switches, folds, pages and menus all animate the same way (or not at all if your system has reduced motion on).

- New tooltips with the control's name, what it does and its keyboard shortcut. They wait until you stop on a control, come up quicker once you're reading them and hold back for a moment right after you change something.
- Four looks in Settings with Dark, Classic (the old deep blue), OLED and Light.
- Settings is redone in the same style and opens a lot faster.
- The phone app is redone to match, with the same four looks and a new Settings screen with About and diagnostics. Paired computers moved to their own **Manage** screen.
- KDE Plasma title bars use the app's colours.

## New

- **Auto** on the Colour grading card sets up the whole grade from about a second of video, keeping skin tones natural. You can still change every slider afterwards. There's also a new **Vibrance** slider.
- **Stats** is an optional card that shows fps, dropped frames and why, the link, delay and the phone's temperature. Its **Nerd** view adds how long each step and plugin takes. Any line can be pinned to the bottom bar.
- **MCP** is an optional plugin that lets an AI app like Claude Desktop read and change Telescope's settings, with a Read only switch and an undo button in the top bar. `docs/mcp.md` has the details.
- Older DSLRs that only do live view over USB show up as cameras on Linux, with focus, aperture and white balance on the Webcam card and photos (RAW too) from the Photos card.

## Changed

- Privacy blur blurs the whole picture or shows the wait screen when more than one person is in it. **Blur the others** and **Blur all but me** are gone and turn into **Blur the whole picture**, including on keys bound to them.
- The privacy wait screen says **Paused for privacy** instead of looking like a broken camera.
- Background covers the whole picture at the start instead of showing the room for a moment before your cutout is ready.
- Auto framing keeps a group framed steadily instead of jumping between people and its levels end at the head, chest, belt and feet.
- A stream Telescope started by itself stops when nothing is using the camera, unless you changed that in Settings.
- "Shape" is called **Aspect ratio** now and "Things in hand" is **Show hands**.

## Fixed

- Some starts with hardware decoding showed garbled video for the whole stream or no picture for about half a minute.
- A crash in the JPEG decoder or a slow app reading the Windows 11 virtual camera no longer freezes the picture.
- The preview no longer shows another stream's picture, and stream tiles keep updating after an error.
- A zoom change on the phone no longer makes the picture jump.
- An update no longer installs over a stream that started in the meantime.
